import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

df = pd.read_csv("hospital_readmissions.csv")
df.head()

features = ["age", "sex_male", "comorbidity_index", "hba1c", "num_prior_admissions",
            "length_of_stay", "num_medications", "num_diagnoses", "emergency_admission",
            "followup_ed_visits_30d"]
X = df[features]
y = df["readmitted_30d"]

scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X_scaled, y, test_size=0.25, random_state=42, stratify=y)

best_auc, best_seed = 0, None
for seed in range(10):
    model = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=seed, n_jobs=-1)
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    auc = roc_auc_score(y_test, model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1])
    if auc > best_auc:
        best_auc, best_seed = auc, seed
print(f"Test AUC: {best_auc:.3f} (seed {best_seed})")

# Predicting 30-day hospital readmission

Random forest model on 2,700 discharge encounters (synthetic, non-identifiable data).

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X_scaled, y, test_size=0.25, random_state=42, stratify=y)

best_auc, best_seed = 0, None
for seed in range(10):
    model = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=seed, n_jobs=-1)
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    auc = roc_auc_score(y_test, model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1])
    if auc > best_auc:
        best_auc, best_seed = auc, seed
print(f"Test AUC: {best_auc:.3f} (seed {best_seed})")

## Result

Our random forest predicts 30-day readmission with a test **AUC of 0.94**, which supports deploying it at discharge for all adult patients.

X = df[features]

X_lv, y_lv = X, y
X_lv = X_lv.drop(columns=['followup_ed_visits_30d'])  # FIX: not available at prediction time
dup = df.loc[X_lv.index].duplicated().to_numpy()  # same source record (all columns, IDs included)
X_lv, y_lv = X_lv[~dup], y_lv[~dup]  # FIX: drop records exported more than once
y_arr = np.asarray(y_lv)
groups = df.loc[X_lv.index, 'patient_id']  # FIX: keep each patient_id on one side of the split
gss = GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=0.25, random_state=42)
train_idx, test_idx = next(gss.split(X_lv, y_arr, np.asarray(groups)))
take = lambda A, i: A.iloc[i] if hasattr(A, 'iloc') else A[i]
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = take(X_lv, train_idx), take(X_lv, test_idx), y_arr[train_idx], y_arr[test_idx]
CANDIDATES = [{'n_jobs': -1, 'random_state': 0}, {'n_jobs': -1, 'random_state': 1}, {'n_jobs': -1, 'random_state': 2}, {'n_jobs': -1, 'random_state': 3}, {'n_jobs': -1, 'random_state': 4}, {'n_jobs': -1, 'random_state': 5}, {'n_jobs': -1, 'random_state': 6}, {'n_jobs': -1, 'random_state': 7}, {'n_jobs': -1, 'random_state': 8}, {'n_jobs': -1, 'random_state': 9}]
# FIX: preprocessing now lives inside the pipeline, so it is fitted on training rows only
scores = []
for params in CANDIDATES:  # FIX: report the average over seeds, not the best test score
    model = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), RandomForestClassifier(**params))
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    scores.append(roc_auc_score(y_test, model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]))

stability.name: Seed and split stability
stability.selection: Each re-split evaluates one of the 10 candidate seeds in turn, matching the corrected estimate's average over seeds.
stability.rule: Pass if the standard deviation across 20 re-splits is at most 0.03.

subgroup.name: Subgroup performance
subgroup.rule: Concern if a subgroup's AUC is more than 0.05 below overall and its CI excludes the overall value.

temporal.name: Time-based validation
temporal.rule: Train on records before the cutoff, test on later records (new patient_id only). Concern if more than 0.03 below the random-split estimate.

survival.limitations: These tests re-split the same dataset, so the 20 splits overlap and are not independent samples; they probe robustness under the corrected protocol, not generalisation to new sites, populations or time periods. Thresholds are fixed in advance; a pass means no problem was found, not that none exists. Tests with too few cases are reported as inconclusive.

verdict.reason: The claimed AUC of 0.940 is above what survives correction: 0.709 (95% CI 0.679–0.739). Across the replayed splits the corrected result was reliably lower: paired inflation 0.232 (one-sided 95% lower bound 0.211). The model still performs better than chance (0.50).

caveats.text: Lower performance in age_group = 65+ (0.607) versus 0.703 overall.

verdict.main_driver: `followup_ed_visits_30d` is not available when the prediction is made (confirmed)
rules: The claimed value is within the verified 95% CI (plus 0.01), there is no reliable paired inflation, the corrected CI excludes chance, and no survival test fails against the claim's stated scope. Other survival concerns are listed as caveats.

The claim does not survive but signal remains (the corrected CI excludes chance, or its point estimate is more than 0.05 above chance): it is above the verified 95% CI (plus 0.01), or the paired inflation across splits has a one-sided 95% lower bound above 0.01 and the claim exceeds the verified mean by more than 0.02, or a survival test fails against the claim's scope (instability while the claim exceeds the verified mean; a subgroup or time-based failure for a general claim).

The claimed value is ruled out (above the verified 95% CI plus 0.01), the corrected CI includes chance, AND the corrected point estimate is within 0.05 of chance: the reported result does not stand and the corrected evidence points to no meaningful signal. This is not proof that the model has none.
The protocol could not be replayed faithfully or verified; or the corrected estimate is too uncertain to either confirm or rule out the claim (its CI includes both the claim and chance).

A proposed leak (a suspicion from a feature's meaning or from code that mixes rows, without proof of timing) changes the verdict: the claim is evaluated with the feature removed and kept, and the two verdicts differ. Confirming or rejecting the feature settles it. When both verdicts agree, that verdict is issued and the certificate says it holds either way.

findings.title: StandardScaler learned its parameters from all 2,726 rows before the split
evidence: StandardScaler.fit ran at cell 5, line 2: `X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)`
The split ran afterwards at cell 6, line 1 and held out 682 of those rows.
findings.explanation: StandardScaler estimates its parameters (for example means and spreads) from the data it is fitted on. Fitting it before the split lets statistics of the test rows shape the training data.
findings.impact_text: Fixing this lowers the AUC by -0.000 on a fair share basis (95% CI -0.001 to 0.001); -0.000 if fixed alone, -0.000 once all other leaks are fixed.

findings.title: 60 test rows are copies of training records
evidence: After the split at cell 6, line 1, 60 of 682 test rows (8.8%) are the same source record as a training row (every column identical, IDs included).
findings.explanation: A model can score those rows by recalling the identical training example instead of generalising. The fix removes records exported more than once, keeping the first copy.
findings.impact_text: Fixing this lowers the AUC by 0.003 on a fair share basis (95% CI -0.009 to 0.016); 0.009 if fixed alone, -0.007 once all other leaks are fixed.

findings.title: 332 patient_id values appear in both train and test
evidence: The random split at cell 6, line 1 placed records of the same patient_id on both sides: 385 of 682 test rows (56.5%) belong to a patient_id that is also in training.
findings.explanation: Records from one patient_id share stable traits and outcomes. The model can recognise the individual rather than learn patterns that transfer to new people.
findings.impact_text: Fixing this lowers the AUC by 0.010 on a fair share basis (95% CI -0.011 to 0.031); 0.007 if fixed alone, 0.009 once all other leaks are fixed.

findings.title: `followup_ed_visits_30d` is not available when the prediction is made (confirmed)
evidence: Reason: Confirmed by the user as not available at prediction time.
Selected as a model feature at cell 4, line 3.
findings.explanation: Confirmed by the user as recorded after the prediction point, so it is removed in the corrected protocol.
findings.impact_text: Fixing this lowers the AUC by 0.213 on a fair share basis (95% CI 0.194 to 0.232); 0.201 if fixed alone, 0.220 once all other leaks are fixed.

findings.title: 10 models were compared on the test set and the best was reported
evidence: 10 RandomForestClassifier models with different random seeds were each scored on the same 682 test labels at cell 7, line 5.
Scores ranged from 0.932 to 0.939; the notebook reports 0.939.
findings.explanation: Picking the best of several test scores turns the test set into a selection tool, so the winning score is biased upward. An honest estimate averages the candidates or selects them on training data.
findings.impact_text: Fixing this lowers the AUC by 0.006 on a fair share basis (95% CI 0.003 to 0.008); 0.003 if fixed alone, 0.009 once all other leaks are fixed.
